summary: Baileys fork: static keyword co-occurrence without traced installer harm
details: The package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web API library. A a static rule fired on lib/Utils/generics.js:395 based on keyword co-occurrence of 'ping' and 'GET' tokens, which are the shape of ordinary WebSocket keepalive and HTTP utility code in this library family. No concrete installer-harm mechanism is evidenced: no read of installer secrets (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, browser profiles), no environment-variable scraping, no hardcoded attacker C2 endpoint bound to a POST, no install-time or import-time execution of remote content, no lifecycle scripts fetching external code, and no dropper or backdoor path. The single-line evidence citation (ping/GET/id tokens) is consistent with the library's normal WebSocket and HTTP client code rather than exfiltration.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
